limits: Only 'G. James et al.' is printed; the full author list is not in the text.
CV estimates can under- or over-estimate true test MSE (Fig 5.6); they locate the minimum better than they estimate its level.
Lab SD over ShuffleSplit repeats is not a valid sampling-variability estimate because training sets overlap.
Does not cover stratified, grouped or time-series CV, nested CV, or leakage from preprocessing outside the folds; bootstrap treated only as a standard-error tool, not .632 or out-of-bag error.
practices: Estimate test error with held-out data, since training error can dramatically underestimate it (p.2, book 202).
Use k-fold CV with k=5 or 10 rather than LOOCV for a bias-variance balance and lower cost (book 209).
Set a random seed for splits so results reproduce (lab, book 217).
Reuse the same fold splits across candidate models when comparing (lab In[12]).
Use CV to pick flexibility; the minimum location matters more than the estimated level (book 208).
For classification, use misclassification rate in place of MSE in CV (Eq 5.4, book 209).
Use the bootstrap to get standard errors when no formula exists or its assumptions fail (book 211, lab).
Refit derived features such as poly() inside each resample by cloning the model spec (lab In[20]).
Use LOOCV shortcut (5.2) for least squares; generic cross_validate does not use it (lab).

terms.definition: The process of evaluating a model's performance
the process of selecting the proper level of flexibility for a model
randomly dividing the available set of observations into two parts, a training set and a validation set or hold-out set
a single observation is used for the validation set, and the remaining observations make up the training set; the n squared errors are averaged
randomly dividing the set of observations into k groups, or folds, of approximately equal size; each fold in turn is held out
a tool that quantifies uncertainty of an estimator by sampling n observations with replacement from the original data, B times

def boot_SE(func, D, n=None, B=1000, seed=0): ... rng.choice(D.index, n, replace=True) ... np.sqrt(second_/B - (first_/B)**2)

def boot_OLS(model_matrix, response, D, idx):
    D_ = D.loc[idx]; Y_ = D_[response]
    X_ = clone(model_matrix).fit_transform(D_)
    return sm.OLS(Y_, X_).fit().params
